approachQuestion.prompt:
Shared Container. Every node of a non-empty binary hierarchy has a unique integer ID. Given distinct target IDs a and b, return the ID of their deepest common ancestor, allowing a node to be its own ancestor. If either target ID is absent, return null.

In examples, x(left,right) denotes a node labelled x, and - denotes an absent child. Example 1: Input: 8(3(1(-,-),6(-,-)),10(-,-)), a=3, b=6. Output: 3. Example 2: Same tree, a=1, b=10. Output: 8. Example 3: Same tree, a=1, b=99. Output: null.

Constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000; IDs and target IDs are signed 32-bit integers; a != b. The immutable tree has child pointers only, no parent pointers, cycles, or shared nodes. Shape is unrestricted. The targets are not guaranteed present.

options.text: Use postorder frames returning a count of found targets and a candidate. Retain a child’s completed candidate; otherwise make the current node the candidate when its subtree first contains both targets. Return null unless the root count is two.
options.feedback: Presence counts prevent a lone target from masquerading as a common ancestor. A candidate already found in a child is deeper than the parent.

options.text: Use depth-first searches with explicit enter/exit frames to find and copy each target’s root path once. If either is absent return null; otherwise return the last common node in the two paths.
options.feedback: Both paths use the unique root routes and occupy only height-bounded storage. Their common prefix ends at the deepest common ancestor.

options.text: Traverse the tree and save a copied root-to-node path for every node in a list. Locate the entries for a and b, return null if absent, otherwise compare their common prefix.
options.feedback: It handles absence and ancestor targets correctly, but stores and copies many irrelevant paths. Only two root paths or fixed-size subtree summaries are needed.

options.text: Return the first target ID found by depth-first search, whether or not the other target is present.
options.feedback: Example 3 requires null, but this returns 1. Even when both exist, the first found target need not contain the other.

feedback.reason: A candidate common ancestor must be supported by the presence of both distinct target identities.
details: Use fixed-size postorder frames. Each frame adds its own target match to the two returned child counts. If a child already has a candidate, preserve it. Otherwise, if the combined count is two, use the current node. Return the root candidate only when the root count is two; otherwise return null. Do not save paths or a node table.

A found target alone is not a common ancestor. Return presence counts with candidates and require both targets at the root. Preserve a child's completed candidate because it is deeper than the current node.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed postorder presence method. Let n be the node count and h the tree height in nodes. What is the tight worst-case pair? Include frame phases, target counts and candidate pointers. Exclude the supplied tree and one returned ID/null. All nodes are examined, including when a target is absent.
constraints: All legal shapes are allowed; do not assume balance. Heights count nodes, not edges.

Pointer access, comparisons, arithmetic on the stated integer ranges, and allocation/release of a fixed-size frame take constant time. No hashing is used. Count all live explicit frames; the method does not use language recursion or copy paths/subtrees unless explicitly stated.

feedback.reason: Each node combines fixed-size counts and candidates once, retaining one live path.
details: Each node contributes at most one target match and one fixed-size combine. Only O(h) live ancestor frames and child summaries remain; a chain can require h frames.

Unique distinct targets make each subtree count 0, 1, or 2. A child containing both already has the deeper candidate; otherwise their first joint subtree is rooted at the current node. The root count enforces the absence rule.
“O(n) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Each node contributes at most one target match and one fixed-size combine. Only O(h) live ancestor frames and child summaries remain; a chain can require h frames.
“O(n²) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Completed subtrees are not scanned again; nesting the control flow does not itself multiply the node visits.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The live explicit stack is auxiliary memory and can grow with tree height.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This is a looser upper bound since h <= n; the height-sensitive bound is tighter and no full node table is retained.
